name: Azazel
overview: The Scripture in Leviticus 16 reveals the role of Azazel as the scapegoat in the Day of Atonement ritual, where two goats were chosen by lot—one for the Lord and the other for Azazel. The goat designated for Azazel was presented alive before the Lord to make atonement and then sent into the wilderness, symbolizing the removal of Israel's sins from the camp. The person who released this scapegoat was required to purify himself by washing his clothes and bathing, underscoring the holiness required in approaching God’s presence.
